reason: Project lens, checked against the source: src/lib/sfx50.6502 is hand-written (only src/sfx_data.6502 is GENERATED by tools/sfx50.py); no PROTECT or PROTECT_BYTES range touches it. sfx_tick runs only from irq1_handler's vsync path in play (bank 5 paged by ROMSEL &05, ANDY out, interrupts off), after the protected T1 write (&2900 us to the palette split), so its cycle change cannot move the split. No data, table, zero page or workspace changes: it reads and writes only sfx_p_lo/hi, sfx_dv, sfx_v, sfx_n in bank 5 as before; dv = 0 skipping ADC/STA is exact (0 + v + C=0 never carries, old code stored v back). C = 0 holds into sfx_pa_c0 on all three entries (BCS fall-through, sfx_pa_clc's CLC then BRA, the borrow path's BRA after DEC). Negative step: BCC c1_clamp0 = old BCS not taken. Ramp end: BEQ/JSR/BRA next = old BNE fall-through. Labels: sfx_tick.down unreferenced anywhere in src/ or tools/; no entries past a label; no self-modified operand in the window. Room: grows bank 5 by 8 bytes; bank 5 end (andy_load + 4089) is &BFEF plain and &BFF5 gameplay/hud_rupture, so &BFF7/&BFFD <= &C000 (the ASSERT). The shifted bench layout already no longer fits bank 5 (grind_config: bench is unshifted). sfx_tick still ends in page &A4 (&A4F2 at most), tables end at most &A5F9+3 < &A600, so no new page-crossing penalties in the tick or its indexed tables; sfx_write's wait loops stay inside &A5xx. One side effect checked: copy_andy_loop copies 16 whole pages from andy_load, so in the gameplay build it now reads &C000-&C003 (MOS/HAZEL, readable) into ANDY &8FFC-&8FFF, past andy_end (&8FF9) and used by nothing (grepped). Front end, define controls, game over, completion: sfx_tick not run there (irq_owned clear) or the same code path; sfx_silence uses sfx_next_ramp.ended, unchanged. Cycles recounted per path: common (no period carry, dv = 0, no ramp end) 31 -> 21; dv < 0 no clamp 32 -> 28; clamp +2; period carry +4; negative-step no-borrow entry +3; ramp end +4; weighted ~5 a channel step is consistent with the measured -14 cycles a pass.
